heading: Wednesday, September 17, 2025
topLine: Genome language models design whole bacteriophage genomes that work in the lab.

items.headline: Genome language models design whole bacteriophage genomes that work in the lab
items.summary: Samuel King and Brian Hie at Stanford and the Arc Institute used the Evo 1 and Evo 2 genome language models to generate complete phiX174-like phage genomes; of 302 designs synthesised, 16 produced viable phages that killed E. coli, and cryo-EM showed one uses a DNA-packaging protein evolutionarily distant from the template. First reported as a bioRxiv preprint in September 2025 and peer-reviewed in Science on 6 August 2026, where a cocktail of designed phages also overcame phiX174-resistant E. coli.
